brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Clear typographic hierarchy on cards: bold filename, muted metadata line, and small tag chips read crisply at a glance.
Colored left borders encode category cheaply and consistently, giving cluster identity without heavy chrome or backgrounds.
Spatial-canvas concept with dashed group hulls and a minimap genuinely differentiates from typical list/grid file managers.
dominant_weaknesses: Cluster placement feels arbitrary: cards overlap group boundaries, hulls intersect, and proximity doesn't visibly map to semantic distance.
Connection lines between related docs are barely visible and inconsistent, undermining the whole 'topic proximity' thesis the brief demands.
Toolbar (Select/Connect/Group/Filter) is generic OS-chrome and disconnected from the canvas's spatial language; no zoom, no scale cue.
fix_priorities: Make relationships first-class: stronger weighted edges, force-directed layout so distance encodes similarity rather than manual placement.
Resolve cluster overlaps — let hulls nest or repel cleanly so a card belongs unambiguously to one group.
Upgrade canvas affordances: zoom controls, semantic minimap linkage, and hover states that highlight a doc's neighborhood.
Tighten color system so border hues map to a legible legend rather than feeling decorative.
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept (spatial knowledge map) outpaces visceral polish and behavioral clarity, since the layout doesn't yet prove its own premise.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — it adopts a canvas metaphor and groups by topic, but proximity and connections are too weak to truly replace lists with meaning.
